# sentry_project_ownership (Resource)

The issue ownership rules of a project. Every project has exactly one ownership configuration, so creating this resource takes it over and destroying it clears the rules, leaving the other settings as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sentry_project_ownership" "api" {
  project_id = sentry_project.api.id

  raw = <<-EOT
    path:src/checkout/* #payments
    tags.transaction:/api/billing/* #payments
    url:https://example.com/admin/* jane@example.com
  EOT

  fallthrough     = false
  auto_assignment = "Auto Assign to Issue Owner"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) ID of the project, e.g. `sentry_project.example.id`. A project slug works too and is kept as written, but it stops resolving when the project is renamed, so prefer the ID.
- `raw` (String) The ownership rules, in Sentry's [ownership rule syntax](https://docs.sentry.io/product/issues/ownership-rules/), one per line, e.g. `path:src/checkout/* #payments`. Sentry strips whitespace around the text, so a trailing newline, as a heredoc leaves, is not a difference.

### Optional

- `auto_assignment` (String) Auto-assignment setting, spelled as the API spells it: `Auto Assign to Issue Owner`, `Auto Assign to Suspect Commits` or `Turn off Auto-Assignment`. When unset, Sentry's current setting is kept.
- `codeowners_auto_sync` (Boolean) Whether issue owners are synced when CODEOWNERS changes in a release. When unset, Sentry's current setting is kept.
- `fallthrough` (Boolean) Whether issues that match no rule are assigned to all project members. When unset, Sentry's current setting is kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `project_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by project slug or ID.
terraform import sentry_project_ownership.api api
```
